observations.behavior: Replaces a large inline Python heredoc and its associated package weight dictionary with an external script reference.
observations.posthog_connection: Moves CI shard scheduling configuration out of workflow YAML into a dedicated reusable script, removing the embedded weights table. This could reduce maintenance burden when updating compile/test duration estimates.

observations.behavior: Defines PACKAGE_WEIGHTS mapping each crate to an approximate marginal compile-and-test duration in seconds; includes greedy bin-packing algorithm to distribute crates across shards while respecting an 8-minute wall-clock target per shard.
observations.posthog_connection: Establishes the runtime behavior for selective builds: it assigns measured or default durations, groups affected crates into parallelizable shards, and outputs a GitHub Actions compatibility matrix. This supports faster feedback loops by only testing changed dependencies without exceeding time budgets.

observations.behavior: Adds pytest assertions checking that plan_shards correctly orders packages by descending weight before assigning them to buckets, and handles empty selections and unknown new crates using defaults.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression checks against expected shard assignments and coverage guarantees, helping maintain correctness as package weights change or new services are added.

observations.limitations: Only P1 chunk provided; no historical baseline of CI performance or adoption metrics available. No tests executed. No release notes or WPR data considered. Tier assignment relies solely on observed code changes.

review.reason: The implementation demonstrates a substantive improvement: replacing monolithic inline configuration with a dedicated scheduling script backed by parameterized unit tests. It establishes bounded capability (selective build orchestration) rather than narrow maintenance, but lacks broader systemic risk reduction across multiple components or critical paths. The tier is not elevated despite its utility because the benefit remains localized to Rust CI workflow efficiency.
review.posthog_relevance: This could help PostHog reduce total CI execution time for selective builds while preserving test coverage, potentially improving developer feedback speed. However, without runtime measurements or wider dependency analysis, this does not establish material reach or production reliability gains.
review.uncertainty: Assessment depends on actual usage patterns and whether other workflows adopt similar scripts; missing context prevents higher-tier claims.
